_comment: V3 CAPTURE -- fixes the truncation confound.

Second family (Llama-3.1 lineage), to check the corrected result is not Qwen-specific. Note its thinking-off mode does NOT emit chain-of-thought, so its off-pass was the least truncated to begin with.
v1/v2 ran the thinking-OFF pass at --max-response-len 320. Qwen3's
non-thinking mode still writes chain-of-thought, so 75% of MATH-500
off-responses were cut off mid-answer and graded wrong. correct_off
became near-deterministic in truncation (0.037 correct when capped
vs 0.944 when not), and the identical probe scored HIGHER predicting
truncated_off than predicting the label (0.922 vs 0.879).
Off-budgets here are sized from the v2 data: complete off-responses
were censored at the cap (max 311/320/319 observed) and MATH-500
answers reach ~720 words at p99. Thinking-on budgets are unchanged.
The capture script now errors above 20% off-truncation, so a still
-too-small budget will announce itself.
Queue: python scripts/dispatch/queue.py expand configs/dispatch/capture_nemotronv3.json
NAMING: capture dirs are {task}_thinking_{model-slug}, with {task} the
task module name exactly. Earlier rounds spelled the same task three
ways -- gsm8k_full (all 1319 rows, vs a 500-row pilot), gsm8kfull, and
gsm8k -- plus lsat_long (8192 thinking budget) vs lsat, and mmlupro vs
mmlu_pro. Those qualifiers encoded capture parameters that varied at
the time and no longer do: v3 captures each task once, gsm8k at full
size and lsat at the long budget. The divergence already cost coverage
-- bench_crossmodel dropped Qwen3-8B rather than resolve gsm8k_full_
against gsm8kfull_.
